dependency_edges.handoff: Reconstructed q(x,t), lane counts and grid definitions feed the conservation model.
Conserved flow, density and mean speed feed physical capacity and piecewise speed.
The mixed-fleet speed relation feeds the induced-demand derivative.
Continuum speed, density and stopping distance feed critical-gap inputs.
Gap probabilities and expected waiting feed the three lane cases and heavy-traffic repair.
Reduced merge speed and baseline traffic state feed shock-wave queues.
Real counts and finite differences feed empirical testing.
The piecewise speed and maximum flow feed branch inversion, comparison and clamping.
Temporal and spatial flux readings narrow the policy use and future data needs.
